q: Who reviews CBAM declarations and what happens if they are wrong?
title: Who reviews CBAM declarations
short: The European Commission and the competent authority of the declarant's member state. The Commission checks declarations against customs data and can spot-check. If it finds irregularities it tells the national authority, which follows up and can impose a financial penalty.
audience: EU importers of Indian goods and Indian suppliers whose data feeds their declarations

ol: Customs data on each import reaches the CBAM Registry.
The Commission checks completeness and may spot-check declarations.
Irregularities go to the national competent authority.
The authority follows up and can impose penalties.

p: The Commission suggests a penalised importer tell the supplier what went wrong. Keep your records ready to answer quickly.
Authorities can ask national accreditation bodies to follow up on weak verification reports.

senseible: Senseible keeps supplier invoices and the emissions data that comes with them in one dated, fingerprinted record per shipment, and its CBAM cost calculator estimates certificate cost from 2026 to 2034. Senseible does not verify emissions, register declarants or file CBAM declarations.
